response.answer: The school seal of Columban College represents the Celtic cross surrounded by the name of the school. It also includes St. Columban's motto "Christi Simus Non Nostri" or "We are Christs not our own" in English. The Celtic cross symbolizes Jesus Christ, the Son of God, our Lord and Savior, who is the foundation of our Christian life. St. Columban, also known as Columbanus, was born in the province of Leinster, Ireland, around the year c. 543. He was educated at home and later continued his studies in a monastery under the guidance of Abbot Sinell of the community of Cleenish in Northern Ireland. St. Columban dedicated his life to God when he was about 17 or 18 years old. He traveled outside Ireland to spread the message of the gospel in Europe, where he preached eloquently and established monasteries that became centers of worship, learning, and service to the local people (source: the life of St. Columban).
